titleStmt.title: Controlled Taxonomies for Early Modern Manuscript Poetry

publicationStmt.p: Unpublished working taxonomy file for TEI encoding.

sourceDesc.p: Constructed from early modern manuscript category lists and Latin genre terminology

taxonomy.desc: Primary literary form or conventional poetic kind.

category.catDesc: Blazon (itemised praise of a woman’s body or beauty)
Contra-blazon (ironic or negative inversion of the blazon)

taxonomy.desc: Formal or rhetorical features that are not stable genres.
Rhetorical force, tone, or what the poem is doing.

category.catDesc: Conflict betwen civic authorities and church authority
Proposed marriage between Prince Charles (later Charles I) and the Spanish Infanta Maria Anna (the “Spanish Match”), c.1614–1623
Petrarchan motif of pleasurable suffering (voluptas dolendi)

taxonomy.desc: Social, institutional, ceremonial, and spatial settings for a poem.

category.catDesc: Household service, domestic offices, and estate roles
Law, justice, civic, and administrative roles
Craft, trade, manufacture, service, and retail occupations
Agricultural, pastoral, and animal husbandry roles

taxonomy.desc: Social directionality or target relation, especially useful for satire and libel.

category.catDesc: Punching down: Target is a social inferior
Punching up: Target is a social superior
Poem expresing a prayer or wish (eucticon)

body.p: Working file for controlled tagging of early modern manuscript poems.
